conventions.formalized:: A Lean declaration path that carries this clause's meaning. Every path recorded here names a declaration the module it names actually holds, and the ledger's existence gate resolves it against lean/** rather than taking the note's word for it. The paths this file recorded at S1 were corrected in this pass, once the value domain and codec were in `lean/Spec/Codec.lean` and the composite rules in `lean/Spec/Message.lean`: a path that named nothing was corrected to the declaration carrying the rule, and the two clauses nothing carries are recorded as deferred with the gap and the code path named.
conventions.informative: The keyword is not a conformance keyword (for example it is used as an adjective).

design_consequences: Map ordering fixes the value domain: the map case is a sequence of key-value pairs, not a set — the constructor says 'pairs in wire order' (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:167-168) — so map equality is order-sensitive except where a clause says otherwise.

Trailing-null omission makes decoding and encoding asymmetric: a reader accepts a shorter composite list than the type declares, while a writer may truncate. Both are latitude, so the conformance relation admits either; the reader's half is `checkFieldList` and the writer's half is unrequired.

Two of these six clauses are uncarried, and both are the same shape: a rule about what counts as absent, where the model counts only `null` and reads the generated `multiple` flag nowhere. They are the finding this file's correction produced, and neither is an artifact of the corrected paths — the paths were corrected *because* the pass that made them resolvable asked what actually carried each clause.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.clause_text: When the trailing elements of the list representation are null, they MAY be omitted.
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.note: The reader's half of the latitude is `checkFieldList` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:365-387): a composite body may be shorter than the declared field list, because trailing absent fields are the encoding's way of saying 'not set', and a longer one is refused. The writer's half is latitude and is not owed by any declaration: nothing requires a writer to truncate, and nothing forbids it.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.clause_text: Note that a null value and a zero-length array (with a correct type for its elements) both describe an absence of a value and MUST be treated as semantically identical.
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.note: deferred: S1 — uncarried: the identity this sentence states is maintained nowhere. The model's own notion of absence is `isNullValue` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:355-358), which counts `null` and nothing else, and the mandatory rule is stated through it (lean/Spec/Message.lean:374-383). The divergence is reachable rather than theoretical: a field the declared surface marks mandatory and that carries a zero-length array is admitted where the same field carrying null is refused, which is the difference this sentence forbids. A carrier would be a declaration that treats the two encodings alike; none exists, and an entry naming one would be false.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.clause_text: A field which is defined as both multiple and mandatory MUST contain at least one value (i.e. for such a field both null and an array with no entries are invalid).
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.note: deferred: S1 — uncarried: the flag is declared and never read. `FieldDecl.multiple` is generated from the artifact (lean/Generated/Oasis/Fields.lean:19), and no declaration under `lean/Spec`, `lean/Contracts` or `lean/Harness` consults it — the mandatory half of this sentence is checked (`checkFieldList`), the multiple half is not, so a field both multiple and mandatory may carry an empty array and be admitted. The general rule belongs in the composite check; until a declaration reads the flag there is nothing for this clause to name.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.clause_text: All array encodings consist of a size followed by a count followed by an element constructor followed by count elements of encoded data formated as REQUIRED by the element constructor:
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.note: The shape is the `Value.array` constructor's — one constructor octet for every element, with the elements' values (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:171-173) — and the order size, count, element constructor, elements is what `readArrayData` reads, with the declared size checked against the octets measured (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:474-499). Its keyword is adjectival ('formated as REQUIRED by the element constructor'), so the ledger kind overstates it; the note records the misclassification and the disposition records what carries the meaning.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.clause_text: Map encodings MUST contain an even number of items (i.e. an equal number of keys and values).
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.note: An odd item count is refused before any pair is formed, in `readCompound`'s map branch: a map that declares an odd count is a decode error with the reason in the message (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:466-470). `pairUp` (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:398-401) is the pairing itself, and its docstring records that the refusal is what makes an unpaired tail unreachable.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.clause_text: Unless known to be otherwise, maps MUST be considered to be ordered, that is, the order of the key-value pairs is semantically important and two maps which are different only in the order in which their key-value pairs are encoded are not equal.
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:types/s.note: Map equality is order-sensitive by construction: the value domain's map case is 'a map with its pairs in wire order' (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:167-168), a sequence of pairs rather than a set, so two maps differing only in pair order are different values. The latitude in 'unless known to be otherwise' is recorded in ledger/ambiguities/map-ordering.json.

scope: Part 1 (Types): the constructor grammar, the primitive type definitions, and the rules that constrain how composite values are encoded.
